notes.title: Arcane Eats is heading to Gamescom and PAX West!
notes.notes:
[p]We’ve got some big summer news: We’re bringing our [b]first public demo of Arcane Eats to the show floor at Gamescom and PAX West[/b] in just a few weeks![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651827/26d85b53897ad3e93cb9ca6d8cd322898fa359e2.png"][/img][/p][p]First up, we’ll be at [b]Gamescom[/b] (Aug 20–24) in Cologne, Germany as part of the [b][u][url="https://indiearenabooth.de/gamescom2025/games"]Indie Arena Booth[/url][/u][/b]. This year’s theme is “Watch Us Cook,” so of course Arcane Eats had to be on the menu.[/p][p]Then the week after, we’ll be back home in Seattle, USA for [b]PAX West[/b] (Aug 30–Sep 2) showing the game as part of the [b][u][url="https://west.paxsite.com/en-us/features/pax-rising-showcase.html"]PAX Rising Showcase[/url][/u][/b], and the [b][u][url="https://six.seattleindies.org/2025"]Seattle Indies Expo[/url][/u] [/b](Aug 31). Hometown Seattle Indies pride~ [/p][p]It’s such an honor to be selected for these events! It’s an amazing smorgasbord of indie games, I personally can’t wait to taste as many as I can. And of course, we’re really looking forward to getting Arcane Eats into people’s hands for the first time and seeing what you all think. [/p][p]If you do come by our booth, please say hi – Bob and I will be the ones wearing chefs coats, aprons, and elf ears. It will also be my first time to Gamescom and to Germany, so if you have tips on good places to eat, could you drop me some links [u][url="https://discord.gg/wonderbellygames"]in our Discord server[/url][/u]?[/p][p]Speaking of, back in the Discord kitchen, everyone’s been goofing around with fantasy restaurant concepts and came up with some real treats. Here’s a sampling:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651827/0dd8d40bc61a3d990a7296ec211b6290cf34255e.png"][/img]
I’m still laughing at the punchline on this one…[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651827/2d7c0019780511b074307693fb69426450768c6d.png"][/img]
So yeah, pop into [u][url="https://discord.gg/wonderbellygames"]#arcane-eats-chat[/url][/u] and tell me about your fantasy restaurant. I’ll laugh at the worst puns, and for bonus points, I’m going to see how many of these I can slip into our restaurant name generator in game…[/p][p]Hope you’re all having a good summer! It’s hot and I’m lazy, so I’ve been making my favorite simple summer dish, nectarine salad. Chop some nectarines, toss with some sugar + salt + lemon juice, rip up some prosciutto and fresh mozzarella and basil and throw it on top. Eat outside with bare feet. No lie, I would eat this every day for the rest of the summer if I could.[/p][p]Flavorfully yours,
Andrea at Wonderbelly Games[/p]

notes.title: Introducing Arcane Eats
notes.notes: [p]Today Wonderbelly announces our next game, Arcane Eats! It’s a roguelike deckbuilder with a delicious twist – build a cuisine-themed deck of cards, cook up combos on magical cooktops, and serve fantastical meals to hordes of hungry monsters. It’s crisp and crunchy card play tossed in roguelike spices with a heaping side of culinary puns.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="PLhMNrP52Us;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]I’m a big foodie and I love games about cooking, but I’ve always felt like there’s something missing. Most cooking games focus on following recipes and speedy execution. Cooking can be about that for sure, but the kind of cooking I love most happens when you let go of following a recipe – when you improvise with the ingredients you have at hand, when you experiment to find new taste combos, when you try to understand the underlying mechanics so you can make your prep work even more efficient or your dish even more delicious. Cooking like that is exciting, it’s clever, and it’s risky – sometimes you fail! And also, it sounds a lot like a roguelike, doesn’t it? Stir that together with my everlasting love of nerdy card games, and you’ve got the flavorful foundation that came together to make Arcane Eats.[/p][p][/p][p]I can get into the weeds talking about cooking – it’s dear to my belly – and from soup to nuts, this game is thoroughly infused with cooking themes. But make no mistake, Arcane Eats is a deep and strategic deckbuilder at its heart. We’ve drawn inspiration from some of our favorites, like Slay the Spire, Monster Train, Magic the Gathering and Hearthstone, so if you like the taste of those games, you’ll find plenty here to sink your teeth into.[/p][p][/p][p]We’ve been simmering in secrecy for more than a year waiting to tell you all about Arcane Eats, and I’m so excited we finally get to share! Now that we’ve announced, we’ll be handing out info appetizers more regularly, so don’t forget to [url="http://eepurl.com/cYbdL1"][u]join our newsletter[/u][/url] and we’ll keep you fed. And of course, if you’re the kind of person who enjoys a seat at the chef’s table, chatting with us as we work and maybe getting a chance to be a taste *tester*, please please come join us in our new Arcane Eats channel on [url="https://discord.gg/wonderbellygames"][u]our Discord server[/u][/url]! We’re hanging out there all the time, and we’d love to hear which fantasy monsters are on the top of your bucket list to make into meals.[/p][p] [/p][p]Oh, and don’t forget to wishlist Arcane Eats![/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2640090"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Flavorfully yours,[/p][p]Andrea at Wonderbelly Games[/p][p][/p][p]P.S. We put our last game, Roundguard, on a deep discount to celebrate! It’s a peggle-like roguelike full of cheeky fantasy and bouncy physics and you can check it out here:[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/848030/Roundguard/"][/dynamiclink][/p]
